# Median reflection deficit and homothetic-fiber cap transfer

Let `(w_i)` be positive on a finite consecutive integer interval and zero elsewhere. Suppose it is log-concave:

    w_i^2 >= w_(i-1) w_(i+1).

Set `M=sum_i w_i>0`. For every integer j define

    L_j=sum_(i<j) w_i,  R_j=sum_(i>j) w_i,
    O_j=sum_(h>=1) min(w_(j-h),w_(j+h)),
    B_j=sum_i min(w_i,w_(2j-i))=w_j+2O_j.

The principal inequality is the exact tail-product bound

    M O_j >= L_j R_j.                                  (1)

Consequently EVERY weighted median j, meaning `L_j,R_j<=M/2`, satisfies

    B_j >= M/2 + (2/M)(M/2-L_j)(M/2-R_j) >= M/2.       (2)

In particular an actual integer center retains at least half the total base weight. The constant is sharp for the two equal positive weights `(1,1)`. No monotonicity assumption is needed: the sequence may rise to an interior mode and then fall.

This is a statement about reflected BASE weights. It does not identify reflection overlap of arbitrarily translated or differently shaped spatial fibers.

## 1–2. Existing scalar reflection input

The tail-product bound M O_j >= L_j R_j and median/product reflection bounds are already covered by accepted fact 97622625586363a7. To match its hypotheses, linearly interpolate log w_i between successive positive integer samples, exponentiate, and extend by zero off the support interval. The resulting function is log-concave; a singleton support is immediate. Its sampled total W is the present M, and its paired sum M is the present O_j. These bounds are reused, not proposed as new results. For the defect identity below put a_h=w_(j-h), b_h=w_(j+h), and

    T_h=a_h sum_(k>=h)b_k + b_h sum_(i>h)a_i.

Partitioning the two tails by the smaller distance gives sum_h T_h=L_jR_j; the four-point log-concavity estimate gives T_h<=M min(a_h,b_h). The retained new content is the defect decomposition and the geometrically scoped cap transfer.

## 3. Median reflection and its exact deficit decomposition

For any j, the shell partition and bounds in Sections 1–2 give a nonnegative defect

    E_j = sum_(h>=1) [M min(a_h,b_h)-T_h]
        = M O_j-L_jR_j >= 0.

Since `w_j=M-L_j-R_j`, the reflection mass satisfies the exact identity

    B_j-M/2
      = (2/M)(M/2-L_j)(M/2-R_j) + 2E_j/M.              (8)

A finite positive law has an integer median in its positive support. At such an index both factors in the first term are nonnegative, and (2) follows. The identity distinguishes the median position from the four-point log-concavity slack.

The tail-product estimate is sharp even for a genuine two-sided tail about the chosen center in an infinite example: for `w_i=q^i` on the nonnegative integers, `0<q<1`, direct summation gives `M O_j=L_jR_j` for every `j>=0`. This example is only a calibration; the theorem above concerns finite sequences and its proof is finite after zero extension.

Every positive concave-root sequence `w_i=f_i^d`, with `d>0` and concave positive f, satisfies the hypotheses: the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality gives `f_i^2>=f_(i-1)f_(i+1)`, hence the same inequality for w. The exponent need not be an integer.

## 4. Existing Cartesian-product input

For product log-concave weights and coordinatewise medians j, accepted fact 97622625586363a7 supplies

    sum_p min(w_p,w_(2j-p)) >= 2^(-n) sum_p w_p.       (9)

No new product-reflection theorem is submitted here.

## 5. Exact geometrically scoped cap transfer

Here is a direct geometric transfer argument, separate from the scalar baseline. Namely, suppose actual compatible fibers are `K_p=c_p+r_p K`, where K is a fixed full-dimensional convex body with centroid zero and `|K_p|=w_p`. At the selected integer j assume, for the reflected pairs actually used,

    c_p+c_(2j-p)=2c_j.                                 (10)

The point `(j,c_j)` then has every original ambient cap of mass at least

    Gamma_d sum_p min(w_p,w_(2j-p)).                    (11)

For each distinct reflected pair retain equal smaller homothetic copies. Their thresholds about their common shape centroid are opposite, so the paired-centroid-tail inequality submitted in candidate 732b11a769399016 supplies twice Gamma_d times the smaller volume. The own fiber supplies Gamma_d w_j; all pairs are disjoint. Pure base-normal caps capture one whole member of each pair and the whole own fiber, giving the same bound. Thus (2) or (9) yields the sharp respective cap constant under the explicit center condition (10).

Scalar log-concavity alone does not supply (10). This corollary makes no claim about arbitrary nonaffine fiber centroids, and the general mixed-integer theorem is not inferred.

The standard-library verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_logconcave_median_reflection.py` checks the four-point inequalities, every individual product-partition bound, the exact deficit identity, median retention, and products using rational arithmetic. These checks supplement the proof; they are not a numerical inference.
